# Results — Study 391 (CEO-Turnover)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The question — **"is firing
the CEO good news or bad news for the stock?"** — tested as a textbook short-window
**event study**: around each dated CEO-change announcement, the **cumulative abnormal
return** (CAR) is the stock's return minus a **market-model** fit (`stock = α + β·SPY`)
estimated on a clean pre-event window, cumulated over the event window. True CEO-turnover
databases (ExecuComp/BoardEx) are not free, so events come from a **hardcoded, labelled
table** of ~25 notable large-cap CEO changes (forced vs planned). Offline core +
synthetic control are deterministic; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every
number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted closes — each event ticker + SPY (public, no key) |
| Event table | hardcoded `CEO_EVENTS` (ticker, announce date, forced/planned), fingerprint **2b48ba1b75f8** |
| As-of | 2026-06-22 |
| Events in table | **26**; with usable price history **23** (TWTR & YHOO delisted, UBER-2017 pre-IPO → dropped) |
| Buckets | **11 forced** / **12 planned** |
| Benchmark / model | market model `stock = α + β·SPY`, 120-day estimation window, 10-day gap |
| Event window | CAR **[0, +2]** trading days (canonical); robustness over [0,0], [−1,+1], [0,+4] |
| Entry / costs | tradable variant enters **1 day after** the announcement; one-way 10-bps round-trip |

> **Two named caveats (on the Signal axis).** (1) The **forced/planned label** is the
> believers' own framing and is subjective at the margin (an "abrupt resignation under
> pressure" vs a "planned hand-off that turned noisy"). (2) Dropping two delisted names
> and a pre-IPO event leaves a mild **survivorship** tilt. Neither moves the verdict: it
> rests on the *sample size* (~a dozen per bucket) and on *where* the only real move sits
> (the un-tradable announcement instant), both of which are robust.

## The signal — abnormal return around the announcement (canonical CAR[0,+2])

| bucket | n | mean CAR | win-rate (CAR>0) | *t* vs 0 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **forced** (ousted/pressured) | 11 | **+1.02%** | 45% | **+0.63** |
| **planned** (orderly succession) | 12 | **−0.45%** | 42% | **−0.43** |
| all events | 23 | +0.25% | 43% | +0.27 |

**forced − planned = +1.47pp**, Welch ***t* = +0.76**, forced-bucket placebo
***p* = 0.246** (share of random same-size non-event windows on the same names whose mean
CAR matches/beats the forced set). Read it carefully: the *direction* matches one half of
the folklore (forced exits get a small relief bump, planned ones a small shrug) **but
neither bucket is distinguishable from zero, and the gap between them is well inside the
noise**. The believers' clean "good news / bad news" answer does not exist over the
holdable window.

## The one place a real move hides — and you can't trade it

| window | what it measures | forced mean | *t* | forced−planned *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **[0, 0]** | the announcement-*day* repricing | **+2.05%** | **+1.95** | **+2.43** | **0.007** |
| [0, +2] | a holdable 3-day window | +1.02% | +0.63 | +0.76 | 0.246 |

On the **single announcement day**, forced-CEO stocks jump **+2.05%** (placebo
*p* = 0.007, forced−planned *t* = 2.43) — the market *does* react to a forced ouster.
But that move is the **instantaneous repricing you learn about only at the close**: it is
gone by the time anyone can act, and it does not persist into a tradable drift.

## The tradable version — enter the day after, and it's gone

| trade | forced mean CAR | *t* | forced−planned *t* | net @ 10 bps |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| enter **+1 day**, hold [+1,+3] | **−0.81%** | −0.70 | −0.47 | −0.91% |
| enter **+1 day**, hold [+1,+5] | +0.51% | +0.26 | +0.37 | +0.41% |

The entire reaction lives in the announcement instant. Apply a one-day execution lag —
all you can actually do, since the news hits intraday and you fill at the next close — and
the post-announcement CAR is **noise of either sign**, and *costs make it worse*. There is
no capturable drift.

## Robustness — the window is the only thing that lights it up

| event window | forced mean | *t* | forced−planned | diff *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| [0, 0] | +2.05% | +1.95 | +2.70pp | **+2.43** |
| **[0, +2]** (canonical) | +1.02% | +0.63 | +1.47pp | +0.76 |
| [−1, +1] | +2.44% | +1.33 | +3.04pp | +1.48 |
| [0, +4] | +1.52% | +0.73 | +2.22pp | +0.87 |

Only the razor-thin **[0,0]** window crosses *t* = 2 — and that is exactly the window you
**cannot trade** (it is the close-to-close move on the news day). Every holdable window
falls back below 2. A signal whose significance evaporates the moment you widen the window
to something you could hold is not a robust edge.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful, small samples are weak

A deterministic per-event abnormal-return panel (14 forced / 12 planned) with a
**plantable forced-bucket CAR edge**:

| planted forced edge | forced mean | forced *t* | planned mean | forced−planned *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0 bps** (no edge) | −0.95% | −1.51 | −0.24% | **−0.64** |
| **+500 bps** (large) | +4.05% | +6.41 | −0.24% | **+3.87** |

With **no** planted edge the forced−planned test stays comfortably below *t* = 2 (it
cannot fake significance from ~a dozen events per bucket, even when noise tilts the point
estimate). Only an **implausibly large** +5%/event planted edge drives the difference to
*t* = 3.9. The control proves both things at once: the measurement engine recovers a real
effect when one exists, **and** a dozen-per-bucket sample is far too small to detect any
CEO-turnover edge of plausible size. That is the entire lesson.

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** There *is* a real, significant **announcement-day** repricing of
  forced ousters (+2.05%, placebo *p* = 0.007). But it lives only in the un-holdable
  [0,0] window; over any tradable window the forced bucket is **+1.02% at *t* = 0.63**,
  the planned bucket is a shrug, and **forced − planned is +1.47pp at *t* = 0.76 / placebo
  *p* = 0.25** — fails the *t* ≥ 2 bar, with ~a dozen events per bucket and a
  subjective forced/planned label. Real-as-a-day-one-reaction, weak-as-a-signal.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The whole move is the instantaneous repricing you learn about
  at the close. Enter one day later (all you can do) and the CAR is **−0.81%** (*t* = −0.70),
  worse after a 10-bps cost. There is no post-announcement drift to capture — not
  NAV-scale, not even sign-stable.
- **"Good news or bad news?" — BUSTED.** The folklore can't decide *because the
  decidable part is unobtainable*: the only reliable move is the announcement-instant jump
  you can't trade, and the *holdable* post-news drift is statistically zero in **both**
  directions. The clean "fire-the-CEO trade" is a window-mining + small-sample illusion.
